stories.source_title: Four T. rex footprints hint at how fast it traveled
stories.excerpt:
Four fossilized footprints are helping scientists step into a dinosaur’s shoes. The prints form the first known set of tracks likely left by an adult Tyrannosaurus rex.

A trackway is three or more consecutive footprints left by some animal. The one for this T. rex spans 7 meters (10 feet). The track spacing suggests the ancient predator had been ambling along at about 1.6 meters (5.2 feet) per second, which would be a quick walking pace for us.

A few single adult T. rex footprints have been recorded. So have trackways from what might be T. rex juveniles or another related species, says Peter

story.title: T. rex footprints show its walking speed
story.teaser: Giant fossil tracks reveal how fast T. rex walked
body: Scientists have found four fossil footprints that were probably left by an adult Tyrannosaurus rex. Together, they make the first known set of tracks from a grown-up T. rex.
A teacher and fossil hunter called Kent Hups spotted them on a steep hill in North Dakota. The first print was enormous, measuring 80 centimetres across. It had three toes.
The tracks stretch for 7 metres. By measuring the gaps between the prints, the team worked out that the dinosaur was walking at about 1.6 metres per second. That is like a person walking quickly!

The prints are about 66.5 million years old. They are not very clear, so the speed is a best guess. One footprint on its own does not tell scientists much, but a trackway shows how an animal moved along.
There may even be a fifth footprint hidden in the hill, waiting to be found.

word_to_know.definition: A line of three or more footprints left by an animal, one after another.

body: A teacher hunting for fossils in North Dakota found four giant footprints left by a Tyrannosaurus rex. Each print is three-toed and measures 80 centimetres across. They are the first known set of tracks from an adult T. rex.

A set of three or more prints in a row is called a trackway. This one stretches 7 metres. Scientists used the space between the prints to work out how fast the dinosaur was moving: about 1.6 metres per second. That is roughly the speed of a person walking quickly.
The tracks are around 66.5 million years old. They formed when mud filled with sediment, turned hard, and stayed behind as the soft rock around it wore away.
A single footprint cannot tell scientists much. But a trackway shows how an animal placed its feet as it walked. A fifth print may still be hiding in the hillside, waiting to be uncovered.

story.title: Liverpool win as Hungary wait on captain
story.teaser: Big games ahead for Liverpool's Hungarian star
body: Liverpool beat Crystal Palace 3-1 in the Premier League on Sunday. The win lifted the Reds up to fourth in the table.
Dominik Szoboszlai is a midfielder for Liverpool. He played in the match but came off after 69 minutes. Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola said his knee was "not 100%".
Szoboszlai is also the captain of Hungary. His country has two big Nations League games coming up. They play Georgia on Saturday and Northern Ireland on 17 November.

It is no surprise Miroslav Klose recognises the value of a true goalscorer.

He is, after all, Germany's all-time leading marksman and until this summer had netted more than any other player in men's World Cup history. Even now, only Kylian Mbappe and Lionel Messi can top his 16 across four tournaments.

But of the more than 300 goals Klose scored in a career that began in Germany's amateur leagues and spanned Kaiserslautern, Werder Bremen, Bayern Munich and Lazio, he reckons all but two came inside the penalty area.

story.title: Germany's top goalscorer now coaches stars
story.teaser: Miroslav Klose is helping young players shine
body: Miroslav Klose is Germany's greatest ever goalscorer. Now he is a football coach, and he is helping young players get better.
As a player, Klose scored 16 goals at men's World Cups. Only Kylian Mbappe and Lionel Messi have scored more. He won the World Cup with Germany in 2014.
Klose scored more than 300 goals in his career. He thinks all but two of them came inside the penalty area. He studied goalkeepers closely, even checking whether their hands were high or low.
Now he is the boss of FC Nuremberg. His team is the youngest in the German second tier, and they sit second in the league. One midfielder catching the eye, Marc Kornwachs, is 17.
Klose tells his players to learn from Harry Kane, who has worked incredibly hard. He says the most important thing is to keep learning.

stories.source_title: Seals long ago evolved to hear above the water — and below
stories.excerpt:
On land, a mother seal can pick out her pup’s cry on a noisy beach. Underwater, seals listen for songs of potential mates or calls warning of predators. This ability to hear well both in and out of the water is unique among mammals. And some marine mammals evolved it nearly 26.7 million years ago, a new study finds.

Seals, sea lions and walruses are known as pinnipeds. They have amphibious hearing — or ears adapted to work well on land and in water. This is “something of a superpower,” says paleontologist James Rule. “They are the only mammals which can do this.” Rule works at Monash Universi

story.title: Seals have super hearing in water and air
story.teaser: Their ears have a clever trick for diving
body: Seals have a special hearing trick. They can hear well on land and underwater. Scientists have now found out that their ancestors developed this skill nearly 26.7 million years ago.
Seals, sea lions and walruses are called pinnipeds. They are the only mammals that can hear clearly both in air and in water. One scientist, James Rule, calls it "something of a superpower".

Our ears are filled with air, so we hear badly underwater. Pinnipeds have spongy tissue inside their ears. It fills with blood when they dive. Sound travels well through blood, so they can hear clearly and tell which direction a sound comes from.
The team used X-rays to scan 217 ears from museums around the world, including fossils of ancient animals. They shared what they found on 15 July.
This amazing hearing also gives many pinnipeds great rhythm. Like parrots, they can copy speaking and singing!

word_to_know.definition: The remains of animals or plants from long ago, kept safe in rock.

story.think_about_it: If you could hear clearly underwater, what sounds would you most like to listen to?

story.title: Seals Have a Hearing Superpower
story.teaser: How seal ears work both in air and under the sea
body: Seals, sea lions and walruses can hear well on land and underwater. Scientists say no other mammals can do this. A new study found that some of these animals evolved this skill nearly 26.7 million years ago.

Human ears do not work well underwater. Water is over 800 times more dense than air, so very little sound gets through. Seal ears are different. They have spongy tissue that fills with blood when the animal dives. Sound can travel well through blood, so the seal hears clearly.

The team used X-rays to scan 217 ear samples from museums. The samples came from 119 mammal species. The scans made detailed 3-D pictures, which helped the scientists work out when the special hearing began.
Seal ears are also very sensitive. Loud noise from boats can change how seals behave, including how they care for their young.

word_to_know.definition: changed very slowly over many, many years

story.title: Seals have super-powered ears
story.teaser: How do seals hear above water AND below it?
body: Seals, sea lions and walruses can hear well on land and underwater. Scientists call this amphibious hearing. Researcher James Rule says it is "something of a superpower" and that seals are the only mammals that can do it.
Human ears work badly underwater. Water is over 800 times more dense than air, so less than one percent of underwater sound reaches our ears.
Seal ears are different. Inside them is spongy tissue that fills with blood when the seal dives. Blood is closer in density to water than air is, so sound waves travel through it clearly.
The team X-ray scanned 217 ears from museums, including all 34 modern seal, sea lion and walrus species. This showed the special ears evolved almost 26.7 million years ago.
The scans also suggest seals are very sensitive to loud noises, like boat engines, which can disturb how mothers care for their pups.

word_to_know.definition: How tightly packed the stuff in something is. Denser things, like water, feel heavier than less dense things, like air.

The source does not say the scans showed the sensitivity to noise. Rule makes that point as a consequence of the findings.

story.title: Seals have a hearing superpower
story.teaser: Scientists scanned 217 ears to find out how seals hear so well
body: Seals, sea lions and walruses have a superpower. They are the only mammals that can hear well both on land and underwater.

These animals are known as pinnipeds. Inside their ears is spongy tissue. When they dive, it fills with blood. Because blood is much closer to water than air, sound waves travel through it easily. That lets them hear clearly below the waves.

Scientists wanted to find out when this clever trick first appeared. They used powerful X-ray scans to look at 217 ears from museums around the world. The scans showed ears from all 34 kinds of pinnipeds alive today, plus other animals like otters and fossils.
The team found that pinnipeds evolved this special hearing nearly 26.7 million years ago. It probably helped them survive as they moved into deeper seas.
The study was shared on 15 July in the journal Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences.

California’s kelp severely declined in the 2010s due to a heat wave and other factors, Linden recently learned. But some of them near Santa Cruz have begun to bounce back. story.title: Teen steers robot to explore kelp forests
story.teaser: Why are some underwater forests growing back?
body: A 14-year-old called Linden Hunter-Pinsky has used an underwater robot to study kelp forests. Big beds of kelp grow in the sea near his home in Santa Cruz, California.
California's kelp shrank a lot in the 2010s, partly because of a heat wave. Now some beds near Santa Cruz are growing back. Linden wondered if those beds had fewer sea urchins, which eat kelp.
He picked beds that were shrinking, growing back or staying the same. He and his dad rowed out, and Linden steered a borrowed robot underwater to film them. He even got seasick!
The videos showed that none of the beds had many sea urchins. So something else may matter more. Kelp forests are home to many animals and protect shores from erosion.
Linden became a finalist in a big science competition in 2026. His advice is simple. Choose a project you really enjoy.

story.title: Teen uses underwater robot to study kelp
story.teaser: A 14-year-old steered a robot to find out why kelp is back
body: Linden Hunter-Pinsky, 14, lives by the ocean in Santa Cruz, California. He sees kelp beds on his way to school. Kelp is a big seaweed. Some beds near him had shrunk a lot, but some had started to bounce back.

Linden wondered if the healthy beds had fewer sea urchins, which graze on kelp. To find out, he borrowed a remotely operated vehicle, or ROV, from a local nonprofit. He steered it underwater with a remote control and filmed six kelp beds.
The videos showed that no kelp bed had many sea urchins. So urchins are probably not the reason only some beds are recovering. Linden thinks other things, such as runoff, may matter more.
This is important because kelp forests are home to many species. They also protect shores and trap carbon. Linden says he had lots of fun watching the fish swim past.

Well, there are a few things you'll need to do before you can make that dream come true.

The chosen applicants will join the US space agency as they aim to return to the Moon, build a Moon base and lay groundwork for first crewed missions to Mars.

story.title: Nasa wants new astronauts for the Moon
story.teaser: Who will help build a base on the Moon?
body: Nasa, the US space agency, is looking for new astronauts. People can now apply to join, and applications are open until 3 December.
The new astronauts could help Nasa return to the Moon and build a Moon base there. They could also help get ready for the first crewed missions to Mars.

Nasa has only 32 active astronauts, so it needs more recruits. Last time it asked, more than 8,000 people applied, and only 10 were picked. One astronaut said, "We have far more work than we have astronauts."

It is not an easy job to get. You must be a US citizen, so people in the UK cannot apply. You also need a master's degree in a subject like science or engineering, and at least three years of work experience.
Nasa expects to choose its new astronauts in late 2027.

word_to_know.definition: New people who join a team or a group to help with its work.

story.think_about_it: If you could live and work on a Moon base, what would you most like to do there?

NASA says it needs more astronauts. It has only 32 active astronauts, and it says it has far more work than astronauts to do it. Last time NASA asked for applications, more than 8,000 people applied and only 10 made the final cut.

There are rules for applying. You have to be a US citizen, so people in the UK cannot apply. You also need a master's degree in a STEM field, such as engineering or computer science, and at least three years of related work experience.
Applications are open until 3rd December. NASA expects to choose its new astronauts in late 2027.

story.title: Nasa is looking for new astronauts
story.teaser: Could a future Moon explorer be picked this year?
body: The US space agency Nasa is looking for new astronauts. The lucky people who are chosen could fly to the Moon, help build a Moon base, and maybe even prepare for trips to Mars.

Applications are open until 3 December, but there are some big rules. You must be a US citizen and have a master's degree in a STEM subject, such as science or engineering. You also need at least three years of work experience.
Nasa says it needs more explorers because it has only 32 active astronauts. Randy Bresnik, who will command the Artemis III Moon mission, said: "We have far more work than we have astronauts."

Last time Nasa asked for astronauts, more than 8,000 people applied and only 10 were picked. Nasa will announce its final choices in late 2027. The new recruits will be part of Nasa's 25th astronaut class.

word_to_know.definition: a person trained to travel and work in space

story.title: NASA wants new astronauts for Moon and Mars
story.teaser: Could you be part of building a Moon base?
body: NASA has opened applications for new astronauts. They will help people return to the Moon and build a Moon base.
The space agency says it needs more recruits. Last time, more than 8,000 people applied and only 10 were chosen. There are just 32 active astronauts now.
To apply, you need a master's degree in a STEM field, such as engineering or computer science. You also need at least three years of related work experience. Applications are open until 3 December.
There is a catch for readers in the UK: you have to be a US citizen to apply. NASA hopes to pick its new team in late 2027.

This is an extraordinary time to join NASA's astronaut corps, said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. The people we select could walk on the Moon and help pioneer systems that will carry crews to Mars.
